    7 · One-call API — quickplot / quickmap¶

    digitalearth.quickplot (alias quickmap) builds a finished, decorated Map in a single call: it dispatches on the input type (raster → field, points → scatter, polygons → choropleth), auto-styles by variable, draws, and adds a colorbar — returning the Map so you can keep tweaking it.

    Module-level functions (api.imshow, api.contourf, …) mirror the Map methods for a terse functional style. This is the highest-level entry point; everything in notebooks 2–6 is what it orchestrates under the hood.

    Setup. Inline plots + resolve the DEM path.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
from pathlib import Path

# Resolve the repo root so the bundled sample DEM is found whether this runs from
# docs/examples/ (mkdocs) or the repository root.
ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "examples" / "data" / "LisbonElevation.tif").exists() and ROOT != ROOT.parent:
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
DEM = str(ROOT / "examples" / "data" / "LisbonElevation.tif")
print("DEM:", DEM)
    %matplotlib inline from pathlib import Path # Resolve the repo root so the bundled sample DEM is found whether this runs from # docs/examples/ (mkdocs) or the repository root. ROOT = Path.cwd() while not (ROOT / "examples" / "data" / "LisbonElevation.tif").exists() and ROOT != ROOT.parent: ROOT = ROOT.parent DEM = str(ROOT / "examples" / "data" / "LisbonElevation.tif") print("DEM:", DEM)
    DEM: C:\gdrive\algorithms\serapeum-github-org\repos\visualization\Digital-Earth\examples\data\LisbonElevation.tif

    Import the one-call API (digitalearth.quickplot/quickmap) and the module-function namespace (digitalearth.api), and read the DEM.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    import digitalearth
from digitalearth import api
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset

ds = Dataset.read_file(DEM)
    import digitalearth from digitalearth import api from pyramids.dataset import Dataset ds = Dataset.read_file(DEM)

    A raster in one call (with a colorbar)¶

    quickplot(dataset) — one call builds a Map, auto-styles, draws the raster and adds a colorbar, returning the finished Map (so set_title still works afterwards).

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    m = digitalearth.quickplot(ds, crs=ds.epsg, cmap='terrain')
m.set_title('quickplot(dem)')
m.fig;
    m = digitalearth.quickplot(ds, crs=ds.epsg, cmap='terrain') m.set_title('quickplot(dem)') m.fig;

    Choose the renderer¶

    Pick the renderer with a module function — api.contourf is the functional twin of Map.contourf; the same levels/cmap kwargs apply.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    m = api.contourf(ds, crs=ds.epsg, levels=12, cmap='terrain')
m.set_title('api.contourf')
m.fig;
    m = api.contourf(ds, crs=ds.epsg, levels=12, cmap='terrain') m.set_title('api.contourf') m.fig;

    Reproject + colorbar in one call¶

    Reproject in the same one call — api.imshow(..., crs=3857) builds the map directly in Web Mercator.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    m = api.imshow(ds, crs=3857, cmap='gist_earth')
m.set_title('api.imshow (EPSG:3857)')
m.fig;
    m = api.imshow(ds, crs=3857, cmap='gist_earth') m.set_title('api.imshow (EPSG:3857)') m.fig;
